_meta.title: Recommendation pilot — everyday AI assistants
_meta.purpose: Test whether the surviving evidence can carry one useful recommendation journey. One category, six alternatives, six criteria. Not a general scoring layer, and no aggregate score.
_meta.provenance_note: Every finding was produced by a model reading a source, not by a human re-reading it. Nothing is marked human-reviewed.
corrections_applied: Portability decomposed into content export, service migration and independent model hosting. Publishing model weights does not make a hosted assistant portable.
Control decomposed into individual control, founder-bloc control and board rights. Two founders holding 52.7% between them does not establish that either one controls unilaterally.
Public benefit compares mechanisms in force on equivalent dimensions. A withdrawn mechanism informs a separately stated continuity preference; it is not an automatic demotion on current arrangements.
Proposed changes are recorded as proposed, not as current state.
'No confirmed match among the researched options' replaces any claim of incompatibility.

claim_types.established_outcome: Recorded in a filing, licence, index or court record.
claim_types.company_statement: The company's own description. True as a statement; the underlying fact may be unverified.
claim_types.commitment: A stated future intention. Check whether it is binding and whether it still stands.
claim_types.allegation: Claimed by a party to a dispute, not settled.
claim_types.third_party_report: An outlet's characterisation. Check whether it cites a filing or infers.

status_values.proposed: Reported or announced, not established as in force.
status_values.withdrawn: Existed and was removed. Evidence about the provider, not a neutral absence.

decision_rules.soft_by_default: Priorities are soft preferences. They order and explain; they never exclude.
decision_rules.hard_opt_in: A criterion becomes an exclusion rule only when the user explicitly designates it a requirement, and only for criteria the evidence can actually assess.
decision_rules.unknown: Unknown is neither positive nor negative. An unresolved requirement leaves an option unconfirmed — not excluded, and not shortlisted.
decision_rules.no_filling: Shortlist slots are never filled to reach a number.

category.label: Everyday AI assistants
category.definition: A general-purpose conversational assistant used for drafting, summarising, explaining and answering questions.

why_this_category.user_relevance: The highest-frequency personal AI choice most people make, and genuinely substitutable — the switching cost is a habit and a subscription, not a data migration.
why_this_category.evidence_coverage: Six providers are already makers in this dataset, and it is where evidence is obtainable: licences are public and versioned, and provider governance is covered by proxy statements and charters.
why_this_category.honest_caveat: Capability differences between the six are real and not assessed. This answers 'which fits what I care about', not 'which is best at the task'.

functional_requirements.label: Usable in a browser without a developer account

alternatives.identity_source: openai.com/chatgpt/pricing/ referenced in search results; direct fetches of openai.com paths returned HTTP 403
alternatives.identity_note: Consumer freemium assistant. Plan structure reported as Free $0, Go $8, Plus $20, Pro tiers above. Not read from the official page directly in this pass.

Official page states Claude runs on web and mobile (iOS and Android) with desktop apps for macOS and Windows. Named models: Mythos, Fable, Opus, Sonnet, Haiku. Plans listed are Pro, Max, Team, Enterprise — a free plan is not stated on that page.

alternatives.identity_source: gemini.google.com could not be fetched (parse error: header overflow)
alternatives.identity_note: Product identity carried from the makers.json record only. Governance findings attach to Alphabet, the parent, not to the DeepMind subsidiary.

Official page presents 'Microsoft Copilot: Your AI companion' with a chat entry point. Pricing, sign-in requirements and the underlying model are not stated on the page. Which provider a user is actually choosing is unresolved, because the model behind Copilot varies by surface.

alternatives.product: Vibe (app stores still list it as Le Chat by Mistral AI)
alternatives.identity_note: The official homepage presents the assistant as 'Vibe', while the App Store and Google Play badges in the footer still read 'Le Chat by Mistral AI'. A rename appears to be in progress. A free tier is not stated on the homepage; a reported 20–25 messages/day free allowance comes from secondary aggregators only.

The official domain resolves to a consumer web chat interface, which establishes the product exists. The app interior returned 403 to automated fetching, so in-product details are unverified. Correction to an earlier pass: retirement of the hosted deepseek-reasoner API alias on 2026-07-24 concerns an API endpoint and does NOT establish retirement of the consumer product.

criteria.label: No individual with majority voting control
criteria.concept: Whether any single person holds more than 50% of voting power and could act unilaterally.
criteria.distinct_from: Founder-bloc control. Two founders with 52.7% between them is not one founder with 52.7%.

criteria.label: No founder bloc with majority voting control
criteria.concept: Whether founders acting together hold more than 50% of voting power.
criteria.distinct_from: Individual control. A bloc requires agreement between its members; an individual does not.

criteria.label: Who holds board-election rights
criteria.concept: Which party can elect or remove directors, independently of economic ownership.

criteria.label: Public-benefit mechanism in force
criteria.concept: A legal structure currently obliging the company to weigh non-shareholder interests.
criteria.distinct_from: Commitment continuity — whether past commitments have been kept. That is a separate preference.

criteria.label: Commitment continuity
criteria.concept: Whether public-benefit mechanisms this provider adopted have been kept or withdrawn.
criteria.distinct_from: What is in force now. A provider can have a strong current mechanism and a record of withdrawing an earlier one.

criteria.label: Independent model hosting
criteria.concept: Whether model weights are published under a licence permitting you to run them yourself.
criteria.distinct_from: Whether the hosted assistant is portable. Publishing weights says nothing about exporting your data or leaving the service.

criteria.label: Export of your own content
criteria.concept: Whether you can take your conversations and files out.
criteria.unsupported_note: Not researched for any of the six. This is the portability dimension most users actually mean, and we have nothing on it.

criteria.label: Migration to another service
criteria.concept: Whether exported content can be usefully imported elsewhere.
criteria.unsupported_note: Not researched for any of the six.

assessments.claim: No single Alphabet shareholder holds majority voting power. Page holds 27.1% and Brin 25.2% of total voting power individually.
assessments.source: Alphabet 2026 annual meeting proxy statement, via reporting of the filing
assessments.scope: Alphabet Inc., the parent. Does not describe governance of the Google DeepMind subsidiary separately.
assessments.uncertainty: Percentages read from reporting of the proxy rather than the filing itself. They are internally consistent with the reported 52.7% combined.

assessments.claim: Page and Brin together control 52.7% of Alphabet's total voting power, through Class B shares carrying ten votes each. Class C carries none.
assessments.source: Alphabet 2026 annual meeting proxy statement, via reporting of the filing
assessments.uncertainty: As above. A bloc holding is not the same as either founder acting alone.

assessments.claim: A Long-Term Benefit Trust holds Class T shares carrying no economic rights, which elect an increasing number of a seven-member board, intended to reach a majority. The Trust had three trustees as of 2026-08-19.
assessments.source: Anthropic's description of the Trust, as reported 2026-08-19
assessments.scope: Anthropic's corporate governance. Says nothing about the Claude product.
assessments.uncertainty: The reporting characterises the mechanism rather than quoting the charter, and notes the IPO prospectus was confidential. Trustee count fell from five in the 2023 description to three.

assessments.claim: Anthropic is a Delaware Public Benefit Corporation, permitting directors to weigh public benefit against shareholder returns.
assessments.uncertainty: Reported from company disclosures, not read from a charter or filing.

assessments.claim: Founders are reported to be receiving a new class of stock with enhanced voting rights ahead of the IPO. The vote ratio is undisclosed and Anthropic has not commented.
assessments.uncertainty: High. The decisive number is explicitly undisclosed. This is a proposed change, not a change in force, and it cannot count either way.

assessments.claim: OpenAI operates as a for-profit Public Benefit Corporation controlled by the nonprofit OpenAI Foundation.
assessments.source: Contemporaneous reporting cited in makers.json; openai.com/our-structure returned HTTP 403 in this pass
assessments.scope: Corporate structure as at the recapitalisation.
assessments.uncertainty: Carried from the dataset record, not re-verified against a primary source.

assessments.claim: The nonprofit OpenAI Foundation holds approximately 26% and controls the board.
assessments.scope: Ownership and board control at the recapitalisation, eleven months before this research.

assessments.claim: The capped-profit mechanism, an earlier binding limit on investor returns, was removed in the October 2025 recapitalisation.
assessments.scope: One mechanism, withdrawn on one date. Not a judgement about the structures currently in force.
assessments.uncertainty: Well attested. What it implies about future commitments is an inference the user makes, not a finding.

assessments.claim: DeepSeek-R1 weights are published under the MIT licence and downloadable, permitting commercial use, modification and derivative works.
assessments.source: DeepSeek-R1 repository licence and model card
assessments.scope: The R1 model weights only. NOT the consumer assistant, and not the current V4 flagship, whose licence was not inspected.
assessments.uncertainty: The licence finding is solid for R1. What is unresolved is the link to the product: which model chat.deepseek.com routes to is unverified, so this does not establish that a user of the assistant could host what they are actually using.

assessments.claim: Mistral is reported to publish open weights for its current lineup — Large 3 and Small 4 under Apache 2.0, Medium 3.5 under a modified MIT licence — self-hostable with commercial use permitted.
assessments.source: Secondary aggregator coverage of Mistral's model documentation
assessments.scope: Model weights. Vibe/Le Chat is a hosted service built on them.
assessments.uncertainty: The licence files were not inspected. 'Modified MIT' is the phrase that matters — a modified permissive licence can carry use restrictions that would defeat the requirement entirely. Model routing for the hosted assistant is also unverified.

assessments.claim: No published downloadable weights for the model behind ChatGPT.
assessments.uncertainty: Widely understood, consistent with FMTI's assessment of o3 as closed. Recorded as unverified rather than assumed, so it cannot be used as an evidenced exclusion.

assessments.claim: No published downloadable weights for the models behind Claude.
Gemini flagship weights are not published. Google publishes the separate Gemma open-weight family.
assessments.scope: Gemma is a different model family from the one behind the Gemini assistant. Treating Gemma as portability for a Gemini user would be a category error.
